Solution: We only know max − min = 5, not the exact min or max

Lower half: 4, 4, 6, 8 -> median = 5. Upper half: 11, 14, 17, 19 -> median = 15.5. IQR = 15.5 − 5 = 10.5

Question Choices: There are 5 data points, and the median is 12. Which must be true? (A) The smallest value is 12   (B) One value must be 12   (C) All values are 12   (D) The largest value is 12
Hints: With an odd count the median is an actual value
Solution: With 5 numbers, the median is the 3rd number, so one value must be exactly 12

Question Choices: Select. There are 9 values. Median = 8, Range = 3. Is this statement TRUE, FALSE, or NOT ENOUGH INFO? "At least one value is greater than 12." : TRUE FALSE Not-enough-info
Hints: Think about the largest possible maximum
Solution: If min = 8 -> max = 11. If min < 8 -> max < 11. Max can never exceed 11, so the statement is FALSE
